newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish army wants case against Moslem firebrand.
newsitem.headline: Turkish army wants case against Moslem firebrand.

text.p: Turkey's secularist army, locked in a row with the ruling Islamists, have taken legal action against a government MP for allegedly insulting the military in a speech four years ago, Anatolian news agency said on Thursday.

It said the military had sent a written request to Ankara republican prosecutor's office asking that Sevki Yilmaz, a deputy in Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party, be charged with "abusing and weakening the armed forces".
The army's petition said Yilmaz had accused it of being an anti-religious body that was under the control of the United States and foreign capital.
Yilmaz, a fiery public speaker, also allegedly described members of the armed forces as "belly dancers and cabaret singers" -- both anathema to pious Moslems -- in the speech made in Ankara in 1993.
An amateur video tape of the speech was shown on Turkish television earlier this week as part of a war of words between Yilmaz and the secularist media.

Yilmaz was not immediately available for comment. He has been in his constituency town Rize since a television station last week showed a 1991 speech in which he appears to insult MPs and attack Turkey's secularist system as a Christian plot.
Yilmaz has said the tape of that speech, which judicial authorities are also investigating, was doctored to put words in his mouth.
